root_cause.text: The RxRPC connection event handler incorrectly requeued RESPONSE/CHALLENGE sk_buffs after temporary errors even though `rxrpc_process_event()` could leave them partially decrypted, causing the same packet buffer to be processed and decrypted again in a corrupted state.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE and commit message explicitly state that “a RESPONSE packet gets a temporary failure during processing, it may end up in a partially decrypted state - and then get requeued for a retry,” and the patch removes the `-ENOMEM`/`-EAGAIN` retry path in `rxrpc_do_process_connection()` that previously put the skb back on `conn->rx_queue` with `rxrpc_conn_queue_retry_work`, now always freeing the skb instead.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove retry-based requeue handling from connection event processing so each dequeued skb is processed once and then freed.
intent_record.what: The code removes the local handling of the return value from rxrpc_process_event() inside rxrpc_do_process_connection(): the ret assignment, the switch on ret, the special cases for -ENOMEM and -EAGAIN that requeue the skb and reschedule connection retry work, and the default case are deleted. In their place, rxrpc_process_event(conn, skb) is called unconditionally and the skb is always freed immediately afterward with rxrpc_free_skb().
intent_record.how: At runtime, received skbs dequeued from conn->rx_queue are no longer reinserted into the queue or retried later when rxrpc_process_event() reports -ENOMEM or -EAGAIN. Instead, every dequeued skb is processed once and then freed, eliminating the retry path from this caller and making connection processing no longer depend on rxrpc_process_event()'s return code here.

relevance_review.reason: The changes only remove obsolete tracing/unused variables and explicitly do not alter RxRPC packet requeueing, decryption, or event-processing behavior that caused the vulnerability.

The change directly matches the root cause: it removes retry/requeue of connection event sk_buffs, ensuring a RESPONSE/CHALLENGE skb is processed only once and then freed instead of being reprocessed after partial decryption corruption.

candidates.rationale: This directly requeues the same skb after a temporary error, enabling it to be processed again even though rxrpc_process_event() may already have partially decrypted or mutated the packet buffer.
Temporary-error handling for -EAGAIN is part of the flawed retry path that permits a partially processed RESPONSE/CHALLENGE skb to be retried instead of discarded.
Temporary-error handling for -ENOMEM also feeds into the same retry/requeue logic, allowing the same skb to be processed again after possible in-place modification.
This call can partially decrypt or otherwise mutate the skb before returning a temporary error, making any subsequent requeue of that same skb unsafe.
This schedules the retried processing path for the requeued skb, completing the vulnerable behavior where a corrupted partially processed packet is handled again.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the core vulnerable operation: it requeues the same skb for later processing after a temporary error, even though the event processor may already have partially decrypted or otherwise mutated the buffer, leading to unsafe reprocessing of corrupted state.
This schedules the retry path for the requeued skb, enabling the same partially processed packet buffer to be handled again and thus completing the vulnerable reprocessing flow.
This processing call can leave RESPONSE/CHALLENGE sk_buffs partially decrypted or otherwise modified before returning a temporary error, which makes subsequent retry/requeue of the same skb unsafe.
